subject.title: Cross-provider fallback should respect provider trust boundaries for images/attachments

question: Should configured cross-provider model fallback be treated as consent to transfer user media, or should OpenClaw add a separate provider media trust policy for fallback retries?
rationale: The source shows a real sensitive-data boundary gap, but the permanent default affects compatibility, fallback usefulness, and disclosure expectations, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Add explicit media trust policy
options.body: Add config, docs, and runtime checks that preserve existing behavior by default while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

options.title: Document fallback as full consent
options.body: Keep current forwarding semantics and document that configured cross-provider fallbacks may receive prompt text, images, and attachment-derived media.

options.title: Fail closed for cross-provider media
options.body: Strip cross-provider media by default and require users to opt back into media forwarding when they want fallback vision behavior.

recommendation.title: Add explicit media trust policy
recommendation.body: Add config, docs, and runtime checks that preserve existing behavior by default while letting users restrict images and attachments on cross-provider fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-fallback history and current blame make vincentkoc the closest available routing owner for the policy decision.
